add.text:
Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""
S1. Yeah.
S2. So your tendency to try to start speaking while I'm speaking is still present, so hopefully that's added to the queue.
S3. Yeah, I mean, the whole thing about the streaming or the removal of unspoken things from the prompt and all that stuff, that maybe that should be put on the back burner because that could be tricky to get working.
S4. And also just complicates the whole functionality.
S5. Now I don't know if it's where the fault is coming from.
S6. Generally speaking, this little playback thing, it's kind of cool.
S7. I think I had asked for it.
S8. I'm not sure if it ever made it into a task or something, as to allow tapping on the, if there's text being currently highlighted, if I tap on that text, then it should pause it.
S9. And then tapping again resumes it.
S10. Also on interrupt, I think, at least for now, we could have past messages be resumable.
S11. So I'm not sure exactly how that works in terms of saving the audio per chat, like bubble essentially.
S12. And then if it gets interrupted, I can go back and click on it.
S13. Yeah, and so queuing up your messages so that they only appear once I'm done talking could be one way to go.
S14. Now the problem there, it's a big risk too, is if I pause for a second, a lot of times I'll keep talking without pause.
S15. The dictation keeps going and there's no hiccups.
S16. However, the risk is, if I pause for a second to think about what I was trying to say, then, and then you throw in 12 queued messages, it's gonna, well, for one, push the chat way down.
S17. So my last message, if I wanna read what I was saying, I'm gonna have to scroll way up to find it.
S18. But also, yeah, spamming a whole bunch of queued messages, just 'cause I waited, I couldn't get my last or my next word out quick enough, is kind of annoying.
S19. So I don't know if it's like a time-based thing where after I pause for two or three seconds, then queued up messages could come in, but also prioritizing those messages so that rather than throw in just a kind of asynchronous update.
S20. A lot of these things are asynchronous updates where some agent responds to you and says, "Hey, we have an update on this."
S21. And then you just throw it in chat and start speaking immediately.
S22. Obviously not while I'm speaking.
S23. I think we already made that clear.
S24. But then, as opposed to responding with an asynchronous update, as opposed to responding to my comment directly, we got to prioritize the responses.
S25. And so the thing that is said first is the most relevant to what was just said.
S26. So whenever there's a pause, it's like, let's go with whatever the most relevant thing is, direct response to what was just said.
S27. And, oh, by the way, we got an update.
S28. And, click here if you want to tell you about it kind of a thing.
S29. I think having interactivity for these voice sessions is useful.
S30. I think that, yeah, I mean, it's a good start.
S31. It's kind of cool to hear the voice.
S32. I know we talked about using the other chat model.
S33. I'm not sure if that was ever explored because, I mean, this one doesn't sound bad, it actually sounds way better than it did when I first heard it.
S34. It sounded way more robotic.
S35. But on a quick other note...
S36. Well, no, I guess let's just go ahead with what we're doing here.
S37. Yeah, I think it's working all right.
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
